Definition: Percentage of national population with access to electricity (grid or off-grid). This is the primary indicator of energy infrastructure availability for ICT. Based on World Bank/IEA Tracking SDG7 data, national statistical offices, or Afrobarometer surveys.
Comments: National electricity access 5.4%; score 1 (<25%). Urban 30.2%, rural 1.7%
revision_notes: Both cited sources verified and fetched. World Bank SDG7 electrification data confirms South Sudan's most recent electricity access figure as 5.4% (dated 2023, not 2022 as originally labelled), squarely within the <25% band. The cited World Bank ESMAP off-grid/mini-grid market assessment corroborates a comparable ~5.3% access estimate. A further check via Trading Economics (sourcing World Bank data) also reports 5.4% for 2023. Score of 1 confirmed; year corrected to 2023.
revised_comments: South Sudan has one of the lowest rates of electricity access in the world, with only around 5.4% of the population connected to electricity (World Bank SDG7 Tracking data, 2023). Access is heavily skewed towards urban centres, with roughly 30% of the urban population connected compared to under 2% in rural areas, reflecting minimal grid infrastructure and heavy reliance on off-grid and diesel-based solutions outside Juba.
